mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it signals accommodative monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital for equities.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in low FEDFUNDS periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.0% indicates a deteriorating labor market that typically precedes economic slowdowns, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in less than 40% of instances when UNRATE > 4.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When both housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) are above their 3-month moving averages, it indicates a strengthening demand environment that leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both above 3-month moving averages
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in less than 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS are above their 3-month MAs, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a high inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 250), the S&P 500 typically experiences negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the Federal Reserve maintains restrictive monetary policy to combat inflation, increasing the cost of capital for equities.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in less than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 250, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of industrial production (INDPRO) signals robust manufacturing activity and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in high INDPRO periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) exceeds 150,000 thousand, it signals an overheating labor market that typically triggers Federal Reserve rate hikes, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in less than 40% of instances when PAYEMS > 150000, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A joint expansion in GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 12-month moving averages indicates a robust economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both above their 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in less than 60% of instances when both GDPC1 and HOUST are above their 12-month MAs, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, strong retail sales (RSAFS) signal consumer overextension and impending economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in less than 60% of instances during late-cycle expansion periods, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.
